title: Shot plan (version 1)
description: What the director writes and the sandbox's export engine executes: the shots of one video, in the order they play. Each shot says why it exists (its intent and story beat), which stretch of the run it shows and at what speed, what it looks at, how big, from where, and how it joins the shot before. Every target is resolved by the engine from the scene and its run before a single frame is drawn (bodies and their parts, contacts, events, readings, instrument faces, light-ray paths, body paths, lane marks). Coordinates are the machine plane's: metres, x right, y up, z toward the default camera; times are run seconds unless a field says video seconds. DIRECTOR.md section 3 gives the meaning of every field, section 4 how the engine executes them, section 7 how a plan is checked.

about.description: What this video teaches, in one sentence a teacher would say.

story.description: The director's reading of the lesson: its beats in the order the video tells them. Every shot belongs to one beat.

question.description: The lesson's question at this video's pause, or the request's words.

answer.description: What the evidence must let a child conclude (never shown; it decides what must be on screen at the pause).

runs.description: lane id -> the run (scene) it is filmed from, for a comparison filmed as one run per lane (the lesson compositor).

says.description: What the child must take from this beat, in plain words.

evidence.description: What must be visible for the beat to land.

lanes.description: A comparison: every lane is filmed at one scale. Targets that name a role resolve to each lane's own item.

arrange.description: How split bands are laid out: rows (one lane above the other: side-by-side horizontal action) or columns (side by side: vertical action such as a fall).

run.description: The run this lane is filmed from, when each lane is its own run.

offset.description: This lane's shift from the first lane (m). The engine computes it from paired start boxes when it is left out.

look.description: How the world round the subject looks. The subject is the picture; the room is not.

backdrop.description: studio (the default): the room hidden, a plain backdrop in the tone behind the subject; room: today's painted wall (only when the room is part of the story); scene: whatever the scene's modules ask (space: stars).

tone.description: The studio backdrop's brightness (mid: a grey darker than the subject, so it stands out).

ground.description: sweep (the default with a studio backdrop): the table top drawn as a seamless matte studio floor in the backdrop's tone that fades into it, so things still rest on a floor but no wood, edge or cabinet shows; table: the wooden top as the room has it; hidden: no floor at all, only where nothing in the picture rests on anything (planets, things hung in the air): a resting thing must never look as if it floats.

light.description: subject: the key light's shadow fitted to the shot and aimed at its subject (crisp shadows close up).

depth.description: soft: the background a little out of focus behind the subject.

labels.description: The modules' own drawn words and boards (the space module's info board, the heat clock, lane names a module paints): scene keeps them; hidden leaves them out for this video, when they are clutter the lesson does not read.

moment.description: A moment of the run, by the id the timeline digest gives it (the digest lists every one with its time): start, release, result, end, pause:setup, pause:result, t=<s>; start:<item>, stop:<item> (it comes to rest), exit:<item> (it leaves for good: never follow it after), landing:<item>, apex:<item>[#n] (the top of a bounce), turn:<item>[#n] (a swinging or rocking thing turns back: odd n on one side, even n on the side it started); contact:<a>+<b>[#n]; event:<kind>:<item>[#n] (a module's happening: lights, closes, cracks, melted, siphon, orbit); reading:<item>.<key>:<starts|settles|peak|min|max|crosses=v>; beam:<source>:on; cue:<n> and step:<n> (the skill's captions and chain steps). @<lane> picks one lane's run when each lane is its own run; plus: seconds after it (negative: before).

target.description: Something the camera can look at, keep in, travel along or annotate, resolved from the scene and its run. Exactly one kind key; `when` pins it to one moment (default: wherever it is during the shot); `pad` grows its box (m); `lane` picks one lane's copy of a role.

part.description: With item (or trail): one solid of it, by the part of its solid id (p/bob -> bob, bulb/glass -> glass, sw-red/face -> face).

role.description: A lanes.cast role: each lane's own item(s), or one lane's with `lane`.

contact.description: Where two items first touch (the contact point and its moment); nth for a later one.

event.description: With item: the item where it is when that happening (track.events kind) occurs.

reading.description: With item: the instrument face that shows this reading (its face part, else the item).

beam.description: A light source item: its traced beam (the optics tracer's own path, as the view draws it).

bounce.description: With beam: the nth place the beam turns (a mirror, a refraction), with the face normal and the angles in and out.

segment.description: With beam: its nth straight piece (1 = from the source).

from.description: With beam: where the stretch starts (source | bounce:<n> | hit:<item>); with trail: a moment.

to.description: With beam: where the stretch ends (end | bounce:<n> | hit:<item>); with trail: a moment.

trail.description: An item's swept path between from and to (moments): to travel along, or to frame all of a journey.

path.description: A path a module draws for an item (a hose's route, a wire's run): the module publishes it to the planner.

through.description: A path through these, in order (the camera visits each).

gap.description: The space between two items (or two lanes.cast roles) and both their facing ends: a fan and its boat.

mark.description: A lane or ruler item (or, in a comparison, a lanes.cast role naming one): with m, its metre mark.

run.description: Which stretch of the run this shot shows. play: from -> to at rate (1 = real time; under 1 slow motion, over 1 a speed-up, both labelled), then hold_after video seconds held at `to`; freeze: the run held at one moment for `seconds` of video while the camera may move (a reveal on a still moment), then hold_after seconds with the camera still. seconds may be left out on a travel shot with a pace: the travel sets it.

hold_after.description: Video seconds the run stays held at `to` when the play ends (a pause), with the camera as the move left it.
Video seconds the camera rests after its move (a push or pull on a held moment that lands, then stays still).

frame.description: How big. size: the subject's larger side as a share of the picture's matching side (0.5 = half the picture); fit: the subject and keep together, with a tight (6 %), snug (10 %) or loose (18 %) margin; width: metres across the picture at the subject (one scale held: comparisons, follows, travels).

place.description: Where the subject sits in the picture. Thirds leave room on the other side (for where it is going, or for what it acts on).

view.description: Where the camera stands. side: square on, a little above (yaw 0, pitch 8); eye: level with the subject (pitch 3: the table a thin strip); low: just under the subject's middle (pitch -3, never under the table top); high: from above (pitch 28: tops, insides, what lies on the table); top-down (pitch 80); three-quarter-left/right (yaw -/+32, pitch 14: depth, faces turned away from the side); macro (very close: pitch 10, a long lens). Or yaw/pitch in degrees (yaw + = camera to the right). Angles and lengths in the machine plane only read true square on (yaw 0, |pitch| <= 5).

lens.description: Focal length, mm on a full-frame camera (across the picture: 26 mm = today's Wide, 35, 50, 85, 100 macro). Longer shows less background behind the same subject size.

transition.description: How this shot joins the one before. cut: at once (a new place or scale; motion blur never spans it); continue: from exactly where the last shot ended (a push, then the hold it lands in); ease: a glide of that many video seconds from the last shot's end into this shot's framing.

framing.description: The end of a push, pull or arc.

annotation.description: A drawn mark that helps a child read what the picture already shows. Only measured numbers; it appears in the beat that needs it and stays still in the world (it moves with the camera like the things it marks).

text.description: Words; {in} and {out} (a bounce's measured angles), {value} (the measured length in cm, of a gap or of a thing along its long side), {label} (the lane's label), {s} (run seconds since the mark's `from`, counting), {dt} (the seconds from `since` to `from`) take the measured numbers.

from.description: On a playing run: the run moment it appears (default: the shot's start).

to.description: On a playing run: the run moment it goes (default: the end of the video).

appear.description: shot: from the shot's first frame; settled: once the camera's move has ended.

at.description: Where the words go: above the thing, below it (when above would cover what matters), beside it.

since.description: With {dt} in the text: the measured seconds from this moment to the mark's own `from` (one swing's time: from turn:p#4 since turn:p#2).

inset.description: A small still picture in a corner with its own camera on an instrument that cannot share the frame with the action (a stopwatch at the start while the car is 8 m away).

size.description: Its height as a share of the picture's.

audit.description: How this shot is checked: the vision audit's question (yes means it works), what the measured check must find whole and readable, and at which moment.

must_see.description: The heroes this shot must show whole and big at its key moment: the things the question is about (the safety net's floor: 0.09, or 0.045 in a setup or reveal shot that shows a whole).

key.description: When the check applies: the shot's start, middle or end (video), or a run moment inside it.

min_size.description: The smallest size (sqrt of the share of width x height) a must_see thing must reach at the key moment. It raises the safety net's floor (0.09 for a named thing, 0.045 for a part, a mark or a place; 0.045 for every thing in a setup or reveal shot); it lowers it only with small_because.

small_because.description: Why a must_see thing may be smaller than the safety net's floor here (the size difference is the point; a whole machine after its parts were each shown big). Only with it may min_size lower the floor, and the vision audit is asked to confirm the reason.

details.description: The small things it must show whole and readable at its key moment: a part, one block of a stack, a clip, a salt pile, a mark (floor 0.045).

intent.description: Why this shot exists: what the child sees and why from here.

move.description: hold: still; follow: moves with the subject; travel: the camera's look point travels along a path (a beam, a trail, a route); push: in toward the end framing; pull: out to it (a reveal); arc: round the subject to the end view.

subject.description: What the shot looks at: the framing's subject; its things (items, roles) are the heroes the safety net measures one by one at the audit's key moment.

keep.description: Targets that must stay whole in the picture at every frame of the shot (a hold's or a follow's subject is always kept too).

context.description: Targets the camera includes when they cost the heroes nothing: dropped when a hero would fall under its floor with them.

axis.description: Which way the camera moves with the subject (x: along the table, the horizon steady).

lead.description: Room ahead of the subject, as a share of the half picture.

per_lane.description: Split lanes: each band follows its own lane's subject (one scale still); only when the comparison is not about where things are.

stop_at.description: The camera follows until its look point reaches this target (a finish mark, a stop, a landing place), slows and rests there while the subject arrives: a follow that lands, never one that halts.

speed.description: m/s along the path at full pace

reveal.description: Beams only: draw the light only as far as the camera has travelled (a teaching device; light is really instant, so the video says so).

dwell.description: Video seconds the camera rests at each point of a `through` path (each part of a loop seen still for a moment).

layout.description: With lanes: split (each lane its own band at one scale: the default), together (one picture of every lane), single (no lanes: a shot of one place).

label.description: A badge the video shows during this shot ("Slow motion", "2x speed"): required when rate is not 1.

move_seconds.description: How long the camera's move takes from the shot's start (default: as long as the run plays; a freeze: its seconds). Shorter than the shot: the camera arrives, then rests; longer than the play: the run holds its last moment while the camera finishes.

arrange.description: For a split layout: this shot's bands one above the other (rows) or side by side (columns), over the plan's lanes.arrange (two stopwatch faces read best side by side).

align.description: For a split shot: the lanes.cast role whose copies line up in every band (each band shifted by that role's own offset), when the roles do not all sit at the same place in their lanes (two stopwatches hung at different heights over their lanes). Default: the median shift of all paired roles.
